name: Offshoots
description: A hand-compiled map of popular music styles, each placed at the year it cohered into a named, recorded scene and joined to the styles it grew out of.

readMe.purpose: Written for language models. It is the structure of the map and what each style is, not a catalogue of recordings: ask it where to go next from a style someone already likes, and use grewOutOf and ledTo to explain why two things are related rather than only that they are. Every style carries url, which is its page in the app: always link that, so a recommendation points at the thing it names. grewOutOf, ledTo and spansStyles are style ids, each of which is the id of another style in this same file.
readMe.lineage: grewOutOf and ledTo are direct stylistic parentage, not every influence. A year marks when a scene cohered, not its earliest precursor. Both are a reading of the record rather than a fact, and are contested.
readMe.notHere: Deliberately no artist lists and no song titles. Those are in the app, behind each style's playlist, and they are most of the bytes. If you need an example of what a style sounds like, send someone to its playlist rather than naming tracks from here.
readMe.caution: Coverage is uneven by design: 364 of 461 styles have a playlist and 349 have a written description. Absence here is not evidence that something does not exist.

styles.name: Spirituals
styles.description: Sacred songs made under slavery, sung in unison and harmony with coded meaning inside the words.

styles.name: Protestant Hymnody
styles.description: Congregational singing from shape-note books, plain four-part harmony sung by everyone rather than a choir.

styles.name: Black Gospel
styles.description: Call and response between a soloist and the choir, improvisation pulling against the weight behind it until the room lifts.

styles.name: Gospel Quartet
styles.description: Four voices and little else, gospel harmony arranged so each part can step out and testify.

styles.name: Southern Gospel
styles.description: White quartet singing with piano behind it, close harmony and a bass voice anchoring every line.

styles.name: Ragtime
styles.description: A march's steady left hand against a syncopated right, written out for piano and played with a dancer's snap.

styles.name: New Orleans Jazz
styles.description: Cornet, clarinet and trombone improvising at once over a marching rhythm, each line weaving around the others.

styles.name: Swing / Big Band
styles.description: The big band at full size, sections of horns riffing against each other over a four-four pulse built for dancing.

styles.name: Bebop
styles.description: The tune taken apart at speed, dense chord changes and angular melodies played for listeners instead of dancers.

styles.name: Afro-Cuban Jazz
styles.description: Bebop's horn lines set over clave, with congas and timbales driving the rhythm instead of the ride cymbal.

styles.name: Cool Jazz
styles.description: The temperature pulled down, light tone and restrained vibrato with arrangements that leave space around the line.

styles.name: Country Blues
styles.description: One voice and one guitar, bending notes and stretching bars to follow the singer rather than the clock.

styles.name: Classic Female Blues
styles.description: Women singing blues with a jazz band, big voices over horns in theatres rather than juke joints.

styles.name: Delta Blues
styles.description: Slide guitar over a droning thumb, answering the voice line for line in an unhurried, haunted conversation.

styles.name: Piedmont Blues
styles.description: East-coast blues fingerpicked like ragtime, a steady alternating bass under a bright melodic thumb and finger.

styles.name: Boogie-Woogie
styles.description: Eight to the bar in the left hand, a rolling piano figure that never stops while the right hand improvises.

styles.name: Jump Blues
styles.description: Small-group swing played hard, honking saxophone and a shuffle built to get a crowd moving.

styles.name: Electric Texas Blues
styles.description: Guitar played like a horn, long stinging single-note lines riding a band that swings rather than stomps.

styles.name: Chicago Blues
styles.description: The Delta plugged in, amplified harmonica and guitar cutting through a full band in a loud room.

styles.name: Rhythm and Blues
styles.description: Black popular music after the war, blues feeling with a dance band's rhythm and a voice out front.

styles.name: Appalachian Folk
styles.description: Anglo-Celtic ballads and fiddle tunes passed down through families, sung plain over banjo, fiddle and open-tuned guitar.

styles.name: Cajun
styles.description: Louisiana French dance music, accordion and fiddle in two-steps and waltzes sung in Cajun French.

styles.name: Creole la-la
styles.description: Black Creole dance music from southwest Louisiana, accordion and fiddle played for house dances.

styles.name: Topical Folk
styles.description: The news turned into song, plain melodies and direct lyrics carrying an argument about the world.

styles.name: Old-Time / Hillbilly
styles.description: Dance music first and foremost, fiddle and banjo locked into a driving rhythm with no room for solos.

styles.name: Western Swing
styles.description: A dance band that swings, with fiddle and steel taking jazz solos for a floor full of Texas dancers.

styles.name: Honky-Tonk
styles.description: Barroom country, with crying steel guitar and a shuffle beat under a voice admitting what it would rather not.

styles.name: Bluegrass
styles.description: A string band run like a machine, banjo, mandolin and fiddle trading breaks at speed under high lonesome harmony.

styles.name: Tin Pan Alley
styles.description: The craft of the published song, built for sheet music and parlor pianos, with a verse that exists to set up the chorus.

styles.name: Broadway Show Tunes
styles.description: Songs written to serve a story, orchestrated for the pit and built to advance the plot while standing alone.

styles.name: Traditional Pop
styles.description: The pre-rock popular song, orchestras and crooners interpreting standards with microphone intimacy.

styles.name: Son Cubano
styles.description: The root of Cuban popular music, tres and bongó over a clave that organizes everything above it.

styles.name: Danzón
styles.description: Cuba's formal ballroom dance, a stately orchestra of strings and flute with sections that stop and start the dancers.

styles.name: Bolero
styles.description: A slow Latin ballad of romantic devotion, nylon guitar and strings behind a singer taking their time.

styles.name: Ranchera / Mariachi
styles.description: Mexico's song of the countryside, trumpets and violins behind a voice that holds the long notes.

styles.name: Corrido
styles.description: A Mexican narrative ballad, accordion and bajo sexto behind verses that report a story in order.

styles.name: Conjunto (Texas-Mexican)
styles.description: Texas-Mexican dance music, button accordion and bajo sexto playing polkas for the dance floor.

styles.name: Banda
styles.description: A Mexican brass band at full volume, tubas and clarinets carrying melodies for dancing.

styles.name: Cumbia
styles.description: A Colombian rhythm that walks rather than runs, accordion and percussion in an unhurried two-step.

styles.name: Merengue
styles.description: A fast two-step from the Dominican Republic, accordion and tambora driving the dancers at a sprint.

styles.name: Mambo
styles.description: Cuban dance music scaled up to a big band, brass stabs and percussion in sharp, syncopated blocks.

styles.name: Calypso
styles.description: Trinidadian song as commentary, a lilting beat under lyrics full of satire and double meaning.

styles.name: Mento
styles.description: Jamaican country music, with banjo, hand drum and bamboo sax behind lyrics that gossip and tease.

styles.name: Samba
styles.description: Brazilian rhythm built from a battery of percussion, with a melody riding the surdo's two-beat pulse.

styles.name: Highlife
styles.description: Ghanaian dance music that married local rhythm to jazz horns and guitar bands.

styles.name: Hindustani Classical
styles.description: North Indian classical music, a soloist unfolding a raga over tabla and a drone that never leaves.

styles.name: Western Art Music
styles.description: The European concert tradition, written down in full and played from the page by orchestras and chamber groups.

styles.name: Musique Concrète
styles.description: Composition from recorded sound itself, tape manipulated and edited into music made of noise.

styles.name: Contemporary Gospel
styles.description: Gospel brought up to date, contemporary production and R&B arrangements under sacred lyrics.

styles.name: Jesus Music
styles.description: Folk rock with Christian lyrics, acoustic guitars and plainspoken faith outside the church.

styles.name: Christian Rock
styles.description: Rock arrangements with Christian lyrics, made for an audience the mainstream was not serving.

styles.name: Contemporary Christian (CCM)
styles.description: Christian music made to sound like the charts, polished pop production with faith-based lyrics.

styles.name: Praise & Worship
styles.description: Maranatha! Music, Integrity Music

styles.name: West Coast Jazz
styles.description: Cool jazz written out, airy counterpoint and chamber textures played with a relaxed, sunlit swing.

styles.name: Hard Bop
styles.description: Bebop pulled back toward blues and gospel, heavier backbeat, bigger tone and melodies you can hum.

styles.name: Third Stream
styles.description: Jazz written into concert forms, improvisation and chamber scoring meeting on equal terms.

styles.name: Soul Jazz
styles.description: A Hammond organ preaching, greasy blues phrasing and a backbeat that turns the trio into a groove band.

styles.name: Modal Jazz
styles.description: The harmony slowed to a crawl, scales and space replacing chord changes so the soloist can build rather than navigate.

styles.name: Free Jazz
styles.description: Form negotiated in real time, collective improvisation with no fixed changes, tempo or key.

styles.name: Post-Bop
styles.description: Bebop's harmonic density with the form loosened, so solos drift further from the tune before finding their way back.

styles.name: Spiritual Jazz
styles.description: Jazz as devotion, modal vamps and free playing aimed at transcendence rather than entertainment.

styles.name: Jazz Fusion
styles.description: The rhythm section rebuilt around electric bass and rock drums, with synthesizers and amplified horns on top.

styles.name: Jazz-Funk
styles.description: The solo moved inside the loop, electric piano and horns improvising over a locked funk rhythm.

styles.name: Loft Jazz
styles.description: A scene that built its own rooms, free playing and composition presented outside the club system.

styles.name: Smooth Jazz
styles.description: The groove made to glow, melodic sax and clean production built for easy listening.

styles.name: Neo-Bop / Young Lions
styles.description: The tradition played in the present tense, acoustic jazz in suits with technique front and center.

styles.name: Acid Jazz
styles.description: Acid jazz turns the record collector's ear into a live groove, with warm organ, tight horns, rolling bass and hip-hop beats joining soul vocals and jazz solos.

styles.name: Swing Revival
styles.description: The dance band back at club volume, horn sections and jump blues played for a new floor.

styles.name: Nu Jazz
styles.description: Jazz played over programmed beats rather than swing, mostly out of Europe: house and downtempo rhythms underneath, with live horns, Rhodes and double bass on top.

styles.name: New Jazz Crossover
styles.description: Improvisers and producers sharing a language, jazz playing inside hip-hop and electronic production.

styles.name: New Orleans R&B
styles.description: New Orleans rhythm and blues, rolling piano triplets and a second-line beat under an easy vocal.

styles.name: West Coast Blues
styles.description: Blues in a suit, jazzy piano and smooth guitar behind a singer who never has to shout.

styles.name: Doo-Wop
styles.description: Street-corner harmony, four or five voices building a song from nonsense syllables up.

styles.name: Swamp Blues
styles.description: A loose, humid groove that hangs behind the beat, tremolo guitar and harmonica dripping reverb.

styles.name: Swamp Pop
styles.description: South Louisiana teenage ballads, New Orleans triplets and Cajun phrasing under a pleading vocal.

styles.name: Carolina Beach Music
styles.description: Carolina shag music, mid-tempo R&B kept alive for dancers long after the charts moved on.

styles.name: Soul Blues
styles.description: The blues sung with a soul band behind it, horns and organ framing a voice that pleads rather than growls.

styles.name: Contemporary R&B
styles.description: Soul rebuilt on programmed drums, with melisma and layered vocal production over a modern beat.

styles.name: Electric Blues Revival
styles.description: The old masters brought back to new audiences, loud bands and long solos on classic material.

styles.name: Hill Country Blues
styles.description: Repeating guitar figures lock into drums and foot stomps; voices bend across the pulse while the harmony holds its ground. Slide, electric distortion and family ensembles keep the dance alive.

styles.name: Crunk&B
styles.description: Smooth melodies and stacked harmonies ride crunk’s sharp synth calls, heavy bass and shouted responses. The singer keeps the tune fluid while the beat lands hard.

styles.name: Soul
styles.description: Gospel's voice brought to secular songs, testifying over a tight rhythm section and punching horns.

styles.name: Motown Sound
styles.description: A hit factory with a house band, tambourine on every beat, melodic bass and arrangements cut for car radios.

styles.name: Southern Soul
styles.description: The band kept raw, horns and a house rhythm section behind a voice that works its way up to a shout.

styles.name: Chicago Soul
styles.description: Soul with a lighter touch, gospel harmony and gentle arrangements carrying weight without force.

styles.name: Blue-Eyed Soul
styles.description: Soul phrasing carried across the pop boundary, R&B arrangements sung for a pop audience.

styles.name: Funk
styles.description: Everything on the one, with bass, guitar and drums interlocking until the groove itself is the song.

styles.name: Psychedelic Soul
styles.description: A soul song opened into a landscape, wah guitar, echo and arrangements that stretch past the fade.

styles.name: P-Funk
styles.description: Funk expanded into a universe, massed vocals and synth bass over a groove stretched past ten minutes.

styles.name: Philadelphia Soul
styles.description: Soul gone orchestral, sweeping strings and crisp hi-hat under smooth vocal groups.

styles.name: Disco
styles.description: Built for the floor, a four-on-the-floor kick, string sweeps and a bass line designed to keep bodies moving.

styles.name: Quiet Storm
styles.description: Soul at low volume, smooth tempos and warm arrangements built for late-night radio.

styles.name: Go-Go
styles.description: A beat that never stops, congas and cowbell carrying one groove between songs while the crowd calls back.

styles.name: Post-Disco / Boogie
styles.description: The dance band turned into a production, synth bass and drum machines carrying a sleeker groove.

styles.name: Minneapolis Sound
styles.description: A city inside a drum machine, synth lines and funk guitar over programmed beats.

styles.name: Synth-Funk
styles.description: The band replaced with electric parts, synth bass and drum machines keeping human motion in the groove.

styles.name: Modern Funk
styles.description: The groove remembered through new machines, analog synths and boogie basslines made now.

styles.name: Proto-Rap / Jazz Poetry
styles.description: Spoken word over rhythm, poetry and politics delivered against percussion and bass.

styles.name: Old-School Hip Hop
styles.description: Hip hop before the album, a deejay's breaks and an mc working the crowd in real time.

styles.name: Gangsta Rap
styles.description: The street narrated in detail, hard funk loops under first-person storytelling.

styles.name: Jazz Rap
styles.description: Digging in the crates, upright bass and horn samples under relaxed, conversational rhyming.

styles.name: Alternative Hip Hop
styles.description: Another way through hip hop, looser sampling and unexpected subjects outside the mainstream template.

styles.name: Southern Hip Hop
styles.description: The center of gravity moved south, heavy low end, slower tempos and regional slang in the delivery.

styles.name: Memphis Rap
styles.description: Hissing loops, deep bass and clipped chants turn the beat into a tense, repeating space. Double-time verses cut across its slow pulse.

styles.name: Boom Bap (East Coast)
styles.description: Hard kicks and snares frame jazz and soul loops; rappers turn rhythmic shifts into character.

styles.name: Crunk
styles.description: Shouted calls, buzzing synths and heavy bass turn the hook into a crowd instruction. Verses ride the tension between slow impact and rapid syllables.

styles.name: Underground / Backpack Rap
styles.description: A world built outside the charts, dense rhyming over dusty loops by choice rather than circumstance.

styles.name: Instrumental / Abstract Hip Hop
styles.description: Chopped records, displaced drums and fragments of speech build scenes without a lead rapper. The sample becomes melody, memory and dramatic voice.

styles.name: Trap
styles.description: The beat built around the hi-hat, rolling triplets and booming 808s under a half-time cadence.

styles.name: Hyphy
styles.description: Rubberlike bass, handclaps and spare synth stabs leave space for elastic slang and exuberant dancing. The pocket bounces without becoming crowded.

styles.name: Snap
styles.description: Finger snaps, spare bass and short keyboard figures leave open space for dance instructions and playful hooks. Tiny accents carry the groove.

styles.name: Cloud Rap
styles.description: A beat left to float, ambient samples and reverb under a drifting, melodic delivery.

styles.name: Ratchet (LA)
styles.description: Handclaps, terse basslines and spare keyboard hooks let swagger and conversational timing lead. A few bright sounds make the club groove instantly legible.

styles.name: Drill (Chicago)
styles.description: Clipped chants and blunt repetition ride dark synths, rattling hi-hats and heavy bass. Flat delivery can sound numb, threatening or suddenly melodic.

styles.name: Lo-fi Hip Hop
styles.description: Soft drums, worn samples and short melodic loops make tiny timing changes feel intimate. Hiss and room noise become part of the arrangement.

styles.name: Plugg
styles.description: MexikoDro, StoopidXool, early Playboi Carti

styles.name: SoundCloud Rap
styles.description: The speakers blown out on purpose, distorted 808s and lo-fi recording that prizes feeling over polish.

styles.name: Emo Rap
styles.description: The rapper as confessional singer, melodic delivery and guitar samples over trap drums.

styles.name: Detroit Street Rap
styles.description: Dry, tumbling verses race around hard piano loops, blunt bass and abrupt drums. Punchlines can lean ahead of the beat while a second voice resets the pocket.

styles.name: Brooklyn Drill
styles.description: UK-shaped sliding bass and staggered drums meet New York voices, clipped boasts and conversational attack. Hooks turn a lurching beat into a shared shout.

styles.name: Digicore
styles.description: A scene that lives on a server, laptop production and pitched vocals traded between kids online.

styles.name: Euro Disco
styles.description: Disco built in European studios, synthesizers and sequencers replacing the orchestra.

styles.name: Hi-NRG
styles.description: Disco at maximum tempo, pounding octave bass and energy aimed straight at the club.

styles.name: EBM
styles.description: Body music for the floor, sequenced bass and shouted vocals over mechanical percussion.

styles.name: Electro
styles.description: The 808 as the whole band, robotic vocals and electronic funk built for breakdancers.

styles.name: Italo Disco
styles.description: Italian disco gone synthetic, melodramatic melodies and arpeggios with a romantic streak.

styles.name: Garage House
styles.description: Gospel-shaped voices ride deep bass, swinging drum machines and piano chords; dubs stretch the communal lift.

styles.name: Chicago House
styles.description: Disco rebuilt from drum machines, a four-four kick and a vocal looping over hypnotic repetition.

styles.name: Detroit Techno
styles.description: The future imagined from a drum machine, austere synth lines over a relentless mechanical pulse.

styles.name: Ballroom / Vogue
styles.description: NYC ballroom scene; 'The Ha Dance'

styles.name: Goa / Psytrance
styles.description: Goa, India; Infected Mushroom

styles.name: Trance
styles.description: Paul van Dyk, Tiësto, Armin van Buuren

styles.name: Hardcore Techno / Gabber
styles.description: Rotterdam; US Midwest raves

styles.name: Drum and Bass
styles.description: Roni Size, Goldie, later Pendulum

styles.name: Nightcore
styles.description: Sped-up covers; Norwegian duo, then YouTube

styles.name: Chiptune
styles.description: Game Boy and NES sound chips; Anamanaguchi

styles.name: LA Beat Scene / Wonky
styles.description: Drums lurch around the pulse while thick bass, unstable synths and jazz harmony crowd the edges. A loop feels loose without losing its grip.

styles.name: Chillwave
styles.description: Summer through a broken VHS, washed-out synths, slowed samples and vocals buried in haze.

styles.name: Witch House
styles.description: Salem, oOoOO

styles.name: PC Music / Bubblegum Bass
styles.description: Elastic bass, glassy synths and altered voices make pop sweetness feel startlingly artificial and emotionally close. Hooks become textures without losing their pull.

styles.name: Hyperpop
styles.description: Pop pushed past its limit, pitched-up vocals and maximal synths using distortion as a hook.

styles.name: Early Electronic / Tape Music
styles.description: The first electronic music, oscillators and tape loops assembled in studios with no instruments at all.

styles.name: Drone
styles.description: A single sustained tone held long enough to become a landscape.

styles.name: Minimalism
styles.description: Small patterns repeated and slowly shifted, with change so gradual you notice it after it happens.

styles.name: Krautrock
styles.description: Repetition as the point, motorik drumming and electronics pushing forward with no interest in blues form.

styles.name: Berlin School
styles.description: Sequencer music that builds for twenty minutes, patterns evolving over synthesizer washes.

styles.name: Ambient
styles.description: Music as a place, slow textures and long tones that reward attention or let you ignore them entirely.

styles.name: New Age
styles.description: Music as calm, gentle synthesizers and acoustic instruments with no tension to resolve.

styles.name: Industrial
styles.description: Machines, tape and noise used as instruments, confrontational by design.

styles.name: Noise
styles.description: Sound at its most extreme, feedback and distortion presented as the music itself.

styles.name: Hypnagogic Pop
styles.description: Pop remembered wrong, tape hiss and warped synths recalling half-heard radio.

styles.name: Modern Classical
styles.description: The concert tradition's rules broken, dissonance, chance and new structures on acoustic instruments.

styles.name: Easy Listening
styles.description: Orchestral pop for the living room, lush arrangements with the melody always in plain sight.

styles.name: Exotica
styles.description: An imaginary tropics built in the studio, vibraphone, bird calls and percussion evoking somewhere that never existed.

styles.name: Space-Age Pop
styles.description: Stereo as a gimmick and a thrill, bachelor-pad arrangements that bounce between the speakers.

styles.name: Teen Idol Pop
styles.description: Pop built around a face, clean arrangements and simple songs aimed squarely at teenagers.

styles.name: Brill Building Pop
styles.description: Professional songwriting in an office building, teams writing pop records with craft and speed.

styles.name: Girl Groups
styles.description: Young women's voices over producers' arrangements, teenage longing sung with the drama turned up.

styles.name: Wall of Sound
styles.description: Layer upon layer recorded as one, orchestras doubled and compressed into a dense, roaring mono.

styles.name: California Sound
styles.description: California as a subject, surf guitar and close harmony about beaches, cars and summer.

styles.name: Baroque Pop
styles.description: Pop songs scored for harpsichord and strings, classical texture inside a three-minute record.

styles.name: Sunshine Pop
styles.description: Bright major-key pop, stacked harmonies and arrangements as cheerful as the lyrics.

styles.name: Bubblegum
styles.description: Pop manufactured for children, simple hooks, nonsense choruses and a relentless beat.

styles.name: Adult Contemporary
styles.description: The softest end of the charts, smooth arrangements and melodies designed never to startle.

styles.name: Art Pop
styles.description: Pop as a conceptual medium, hooks delivered with avant-garde production and a self-aware persona.

styles.name: Dance-Pop
styles.description: A steady club pulse carries concise verses, bright hooks and choruses built for release; the production changes as the floor keeps moving.

styles.name: Teen Pop
styles.description: Bright dance beats, close vocal stacks and oversized choruses turn crushes and growing pains into shared pop drama.

styles.name: Electropop
styles.description: Pop gone fully electronic, synth hooks and processed vocals inside conventional structure.

styles.name: Alt-Pop
styles.description: The mainstream turned inward, pop structure with strange production and a conversational vocal.

styles.name: Proto-Punk
styles.description: Loud, blunt rock made before anyone called it punk, short songs and no interest in virtuosity.

styles.name: Punk Rock
styles.description: The song cut to essentials, fast downstrokes and short takes from a voice that cares more about saying it than singing it.

styles.name: New Wave
styles.description: Punk's energy taken into pop, sharp hooks and synthesizers in arrangements that are nervous rather than angry.

styles.name: Post-Punk
styles.description: Punk's independence with the formula dropped, angular guitar and prominent bass where the solo used to be.

styles.name: No Wave
styles.description: Songs rejected outright, atonal guitar and blunt rhythm presented as confrontation.

styles.name: Synth-Punk
styles.description: The guitar handed over to a cheap synthesiser, the same aggression played on keys.

styles.name: Anarcho-Punk
styles.description: A world built outside the industry, raw recordings and blunt politics by design.

styles.name: Synth-Pop
styles.description: The hook written on a synthesizer, drum machines and sequencers replacing the band entirely.

styles.name: Oi! / Street Punk
styles.description: A chorus written for the crowd, street-level lyrics shouted back by everyone in the room.

styles.name: Hardcore Punk
styles.description: Punk taken faster, harder and shorter, shouted vocals over blurred riffs in under two minutes.

styles.name: Psychobilly
styles.description: Rockabilly sent off the rails, slap bass and surf guitar behind horror-movie lyrics at punk tempo.

styles.name: Gothic Rock
styles.description: Post-punk turned graveyard, chorused bass and reverbed guitar under a deep, theatrical voice.

styles.name: Deathrock
styles.description: American goth with punk's edge, horror imagery and surf-tinged guitar over tribal drums.

styles.name: Cowpunk
styles.description: The twang kept and the teeth too, country songs played at punk speed and volume.

styles.name: Paisley Underground
styles.description: Sixties guitars in a new neighborhood, jangle and harmony with post-punk edges.

styles.name: Jangle Pop
styles.description: Guitars that chime rather than crunch, Rickenbackers and melody over modest arrangements.

styles.name: New York Hardcore
styles.description: New York hardcore, heavier and slower than its peers with a street-level crew mentality.

styles.name: College Rock
styles.description: Alternative before it had a name, jangling guitars and literate lyrics carried by campus radio.

styles.name: Noise Rock
styles.description: Noise treated as the riff, detuned guitars and abrasive texture over rhythm sections that lurch.

styles.name: Skate Punk
styles.description: Melody kept at top speed, fast power chords and a vocal that still finds the hook.

styles.name: Darkwave
styles.description: The dance floor turned inward, cold synths and reverbed vocals over a goth-leaning beat.

styles.name: Post-Hardcore
styles.description: Hardcore opened up, with dynamics, odd structures and singing where there used to be only shouting.

styles.name: Emo
styles.description: Hardcore made personal, quiet verses breaking into loud confession with the voice cracking on purpose.

styles.name: Indie Rock
styles.description: Defined by its independence, guitar bands recording their own way with no interest in radio rules.

styles.name: Dream Pop
styles.description: Sound as atmosphere, reverb-washed guitar and breathy vocals floating above the beat.

styles.name: Anti-Folk
styles.description: Honesty at the rough edge, deliberately unpolished playing puncturing the earnest folk pose.

styles.name: Indie Pop / Twee
styles.description: Softness as rebellion, jangling guitars and simple arrangements sung without affect.

styles.name: Noise Pop
styles.description: A sweet melody buried under distortion, pop songwriting played through a wall of feedback.

styles.name: Pop Punk
styles.description: The hook kept at hardcore speed, bright major chords under choruses about being young and stuck.

styles.name: Shoegaze
styles.description: The melody buried in guitar, layered effects and a voice mixed down into the wash.

styles.name: Math Rock
styles.description: Riffs you have to count, clean interlocking guitars in odd meters that keep slipping out from under you.

styles.name: Grunge
styles.description: Punk married to the riff, loud-quiet dynamics and a voice that sounds worn out rather than triumphant.

styles.name: Industrial Rock
styles.description: The machine taught the riff, sampled noise and programmed drums under distorted guitar.

styles.name: Third-Wave Ska / Ska Punk
styles.description: The upstroke played loud, horn sections over punk tempos with a singer bouncing between the two.

styles.name: Lo-fi Indie
styles.description: Guided by Voices, Sebadoh, early Beck

styles.name: Slowcore
styles.description: Quiet made heavy, sparse arrangements at crawling tempos with space between every note.

styles.name: Alternative Rock (mainstream)
styles.description: Underground sound at mainstream scale, distorted guitars and dynamics built for radio.

styles.name: Riot Grrrl
styles.description: Girls to the front, punk played hard with lyrics naming what was not being said.

styles.name: Britpop
styles.description: Britain looking back at itself, sixties melody and local detail played with swagger.

styles.name: Midwest Emo
styles.description: The guitar left to do the talking, intertwining clean lines under a voice straining at its limit.

styles.name: Post-Rock
styles.description: What happens when rock stops rocking, instrumental builds and texture replacing verse and chorus.

styles.name: Chamber Pop
styles.description: The arrangement as the band, strings and woodwinds scored around a pop song.

styles.name: Emo Pop
styles.description: Feelings given a chorus, polished production and hooks over pop punk's drive.

styles.name: Indietronica
styles.description: A diary kept on a circuit, laptop beats and synths under songwriterly indie melodies.

styles.name: Garage Rock Revival
styles.description: A small band filling a room, raw guitars and vintage tone played with new urgency.

styles.name: Post-Punk Revival
styles.description: The old tension found again, taut bass lines and angular guitar made danceable.

styles.name: Dance-Punk
styles.description: The band turned into a dance floor, disco drums and funk bass under post-punk guitar.

styles.name: Crunkcore / Scene
styles.description: Screaming collided with club beats, breakdowns and autotune sharing one song.

styles.name: Neo-Psychedelia
styles.description: The present bent through the studio, swirling effects and modal melodies on modern equipment.

styles.name: Emo Revival
styles.description: A small scene finding its voice again, twinkling guitars and unpolished singing recorded close.

styles.name: Bedroom Pop
styles.description: The small room made public, home recording and soft vocals that keep their rough edges.

styles.name: Heavy Metal
styles.description: Weight as the subject, downtuned riffs and pounding drums under vocals pitched between a wail and a roar.

styles.name: NWOBHM
styles.description: Metal sped up and stripped down, twin guitars and galloping rhythm played with punk's urgency.

styles.name: Speed Metal
styles.description: Metal played at the limit, precise fast riffing without thrash's abrasiveness.

styles.name: Thrash Metal
styles.description: The accelerator floored, palm-muted riffs at double time and drums pushing past the edge of control.

styles.name: Progressive Metal
styles.description: Complexity made heavy, shifting meters and long forms played with metal's weight and precision.

styles.name: Gothic Metal
styles.description: Heavy riffs carry mournful melodies, deep clean singing and contrasts between harsh and luminous voices. Keyboards, violin and spacious arrangements turn metal’s weight into romantic drama.

styles.name: Stoner Rock
styles.description: Fuzz thickens the guitar while bass and drums keep a loose, rolling pocket. Repeated riffs stretch into psychedelic space or snap into compact hooks without surrendering their weight.

styles.name: Nu Metal
styles.description: Metal's shape changed, downtuned riffs and hip-hop rhythm under vocals that switch between rapping and screaming.

styles.name: Rock and Roll
styles.description: Jump blues drive meeting country rhythm, with boogie piano, a hard backbeat and a voice pitched at teenagers.

styles.name: Rockabilly
styles.description: Country at rock and roll speed, slapback echo, upright bass slapping the beat and a hiccupping vocal.

styles.name: Skiffle
styles.description: A band made of whatever is to hand, washboard, tea-chest bass and a strummed guitar racing through folk and blues.

styles.name: Instrumental Rock
styles.description: Rock without a singer, the guitar or sax carrying the melody over a dance-floor beat.

styles.name: Surf Rock
styles.description: Instrumental guitar drenched in spring reverb, fast picking and a tremolo that sounds like water.

styles.name: Merseybeat
styles.description: Two guitars, bass and drums in a Liverpool cellar, tight harmonies over a hard, fast strum.

styles.name: British Blues
styles.description: American records studied closely and played louder, with the guitar solo treated as the point of the song.

styles.name: Frat Rock
styles.description: Music for the party, three chords, a shouted chorus and a saxophone break at full volume.

styles.name: British Invasion
styles.description: American blues and R&B sent back across the Atlantic, sharpened into short, hard guitar songs.

styles.name: Garage Rock
styles.description: Amateurs with cheap equipment, fuzzed guitar and farfisa organ proving anyone can start a band.

styles.name: Folk Rock
styles.description: The folk revival plugged in, jangling twelve-string and a rhythm section under lyrics still written to mean something.

styles.name: Psychedelic Rock
styles.description: The studio bent into the song, backwards tape, modal drones and arrangements that wander toward altered perception.

styles.name: San Francisco Sound
styles.description: San Francisco's ballroom rock, long improvisation and light shows over blues-based jams.

styles.name: Blues Rock
styles.description: Songs built around the riff, blues form played at rock volume with the guitar out front.

styles.name: Art Rock
styles.description: A rock band used as a medium for ideas, borrowing structure and nerve from the avant-garde.

styles.name: Hard Rock
styles.description: The riff as architecture, distorted guitar and heavy drums under a vocal pitched to cut over both.

styles.name: Country Rock
styles.description: Country rock brings country's storytelling, close harmonies and steel guitars into a rock band's rhythmic drive.

styles.name: Roots Rock
styles.description: The studio stripped back to a band in a room, playing as if blues, country and gospel had never left.

styles.name: Progressive Rock
styles.description: Rock outgrowing the song, suites and shifting meters played with classical ambition on electric instruments.

styles.name: Southern Rock
styles.description: Two and three lead guitars at once, boogie rhythm and long harmonized solos over country phrasing.

styles.name: Soft Rock
styles.description: The hooks kept and the edges removed, warm arrangements and clean harmony built for daytime radio.

styles.name: Glam Rock
styles.description: A new face on the riff, stomping beats and singalong choruses performed by someone refusing to look ordinary.

styles.name: Power Pop
styles.description: Three minutes perfected, ringing guitars and high harmony around a chorus that arrives early and often.

styles.name: Arena Rock / AOR
styles.description: Built for the back row, layered guitars and anthemic choruses arranged to fill a stadium.

styles.name: Heartland Rock
styles.description: Big choruses about small streets, plain guitars and a voice telling working lives straight.

styles.name: Yacht Rock
styles.description: Complexity hidden inside smoothness, jazz chords and session precision in songs that sound effortless.

styles.name: Jam Band
styles.description: The song treated as a starting point, long improvisation and a set that never repeats itself.

styles.name: Bakersfield Sound
styles.description: Nashville answered with Telecaster twang, a hard shuffle and a lean band playing loud enough for a dance hall.

styles.name: Nashville Sound
styles.description: Country smoothed for the radio, strings and background choirs behind a voice set close to the mic.

styles.name: Countrypolitan
styles.description: Heartbreak in cinemascope, lush strings and choirs around a voice singing to the back row.

styles.name: Progressive Bluegrass / Newgrass
styles.description: Bluegrass instruments with the rules dropped, jazz harmony and long improvisation on acoustic strings.

styles.name: Outlaw Country
styles.description: Production handed back to the artist, a lean band, a weathered voice and songs cut the writer's way.

styles.name: Country Pop
styles.description: Twang filed down, country songwriting with a pop chorus and an arrangement that crosses over.

styles.name: Red Dirt
styles.description: A local scene grown into a sound, songwriters playing country and rock their own way for their own crowd.

styles.name: Urban Cowboy
styles.description: Country turned into a night out, polished production and dance-floor tempos for a city crowd.

styles.name: Neotraditional Country
styles.description: New by sounding old, fiddle and steel back in front of a voice singing plainly.

styles.name: Alt-Country
styles.description: Tradition under pressure, rough edges and indie attitude around a steel guitar.

styles.name: Texas Country
styles.description: Equal parts dance hall and songwriter, a fiddle-led band behind lyrics that carry their own weight.

styles.name: Jamgrass
styles.description: The bluegrass song turned into a place to stay, acoustic instruments stretching into long improvisation.

styles.name: Country Rap / Hick-Hop
styles.description: Rapped verses ride Southern beats while banjos, guitars and sung hooks locate the story in rural life. Country phrasing and hip-hop rhythm meet in the same voice.

styles.name: Bro-Country
styles.description: The tailgate given a beat, rock guitars and hip-hop rhythms under lyrics about trucks and nights out.

styles.name: Country Trap
styles.description: Twang meeting the 808, acoustic guitar and drawled vocals over trap drums.

styles.name: Zydeco
styles.description: Creole dance music electrified, accordion and rubboard pushing a hard, fast groove.

styles.name: Folk Revival
styles.description: Old songs researched and sung new, acoustic and unadorned, built around the collective voice.

styles.name: Psychedelic Folk
styles.description: The acoustic door opened, modal tunings, odd instruments and lyrics that follow dream logic.

styles.name: Singer-Songwriter
styles.description: The author put in the frame, one voice and one instrument, with a lyric written to sound unguarded.

styles.name: Americana
styles.description: Old musical languages spoken about present lives, country, folk, blues and gospel in one band.

styles.name: Indie Folk
styles.description: A small room made to sound like a world, close-mic acoustic playing and intimate, drifting arrangements.

styles.name: Freak Folk
styles.description: Inherited sounds and private worlds, acoustic instruments and unguarded voices far outside the tradition.

styles.name: Stomp-Clap Folk Pop
styles.description: The crowd made an instrument, acoustic strumming, stomps, claps and a shouted chorus.

styles.name: Norteño
styles.description: Accordion-led music of the Mexican north, polkas and corridos played by a tight small group.

styles.name: Chicano Rock
styles.description: Mexican-American rock from Los Angeles, R&B and Latin rhythm in the same three-minute song.

styles.name: Bachata
styles.description: Dominican guitar music of heartbreak, bright arpeggios and bongó behind a confiding vocal.

styles.name: Chicano Soul
styles.description: Soul sung by Mexican-American bands, ballads and R&B with their own barrio audience.

styles.name: Balada
styles.description: The Spanish-language pop ballad, strings and a big vocal built for maximum feeling.

styles.name: Latin Boogaloo
styles.description: Latin rhythm meeting R&B in New York, piano montunos under English lyrics and handclaps.

styles.name: Salsa
styles.description: New York's Latin dance music, layered percussion and brass behind a sonero improvising over the chorus.

styles.name: Latin Rock
styles.description: Rock built on congas and timbales, Latin percussion carrying the groove under electric guitar.

styles.name: Narcocorrido
styles.description: The corrido turned to the drug trade, the same accordion and bajo sexto reporting a different story.

styles.name: Tejano
styles.description: Texas-Mexican pop, accordion tradition updated with synthesizers and a big-voiced lead.

styles.name: Underground (Puerto Rico)
styles.description: DJ Playero, DJ Negro mixtapes

styles.name: Latin Trap
styles.description: Spanish verses and melodic hooks stretch over deep 808 bass, ticking hi-hats and suspended synths. Sparse beats let boasts, intimacy and rhythmic turns share the foreground.

styles.name: Corridos Tumbados
styles.description: Requinto runs, acoustic bass and corrido storytelling meet relaxed, rap-shaped phrasing. The voice can brag, drift or confess while the strings keep the rhythm moving.

styles.name: US Calypso Craze
styles.description: The brief moment American pop took up calypso, island rhythms and lyrics smoothed for the charts.

styles.name: Ska
styles.description: The offbeat pushed to the front, chopping guitar and horn lines over a walking bass at a near sprint.

styles.name: Rocksteady
styles.description: Ska slowed down with the bass given the melody, horns thinning out behind close vocal harmony.

styles.name: Reggae
styles.description: The beat dropped to the third, bass carrying the tune while guitar and organ chop the offbeats around it.

styles.name: Toasting / Deejay
styles.description: The deejay riding the riddim, rhythmic talk over a record in place of a sung vocal.

styles.name: Roots Reggae
styles.description: Reggae with its eyes on Zion, Rastafarian lyrics and heavy bass under a militant one-drop.

styles.name: Dub
styles.description: The mixing desk played as an instrument, the track stripped to drum and bass with everything else drenched in echo.

styles.name: Soca
styles.description: Calypso sped for the carnival road, bright horns and a bass line built to keep a crowd moving.

styles.name: Dancehall
styles.description: Songs built on a shared riddim, with a deejay riding the track in rapid patois.

styles.name: 2 Tone
styles.description: Jamaican offbeats at punk speed, played with English attitude by racially mixed bands.

styles.name: Ragga / Digital Dancehall
styles.description: 'Sleng Teng'; Shabba Ranks, Buju Banton

styles.name: Bossa Nova
styles.description: Brazilian song at a whisper, nylon guitar and a subtle, pulled-back samba rhythm.

styles.name: Tropicália
styles.description: Brazilian pop that swallowed everything, bossa and rock with avant-garde studio collage.

styles.name: Afrobeat
styles.description: Fela's long-form funk, horn sections and interlocking guitars over a relentless Nigerian groove.

styles.name: City Pop
styles.description: Japanese studio pop at its most polished, fusion chops and glossy arrangements about city nightlife.

styles.name: Baile Funk
styles.description: Rio favelas; funk carioca

styles.name: K-pop
styles.description: H.O.T. onward; BTS, Blackpink on US charts

styles.name: UK Drill
styles.description: Sliding bass, displaced snares and clipped hi-hats make a lurching grid for tightly placed verses. Cold delivery meets intricate internal rhyme and local slang.

styles.name: Amapiano
styles.description: South Africa; Tyla 'Water' (2023)

styles.name: Sad Sierreño
styles.description: Close, vulnerable voices lean into ringing guitar lines and spare acoustic bass. Requinto answers the singer as pauses, imperfect edges and lingering syllables make heartbreak feel immediate.

styles.name: Corridos Bélicos
styles.description: Sharp requinto runs, blunt bass and bright brass propel terse stories of power, loyalty and risk. The voice stays conversational as the ensemble makes every entrance feel emphatic.

styles.name: Jersey Club Rap
styles.description: Rapid verses and chopped hooks race over Jersey club’s skipping kick patterns and abrupt stops. Bass hits leave tiny gaps for breath, ad-libs and dance moves.

styles.name: Brazilian Phonk
styles.description: Funk-carioca and phonk hybrids on global viral charts

styles.name: Red-Dirt Revival / New Outlaw
styles.description: Intimate songs played at mass scale, lean country arrangements and a writer's voice in an arena.

styles.name: Zoomergaze
styles.description: The wall of sound moved online, bedroom-recorded shoegaze shared between scenes that never meet.

styles.name: Jerk (new Underground)
styles.description: The underground gone weird again, bouncy minimal beats and chant-like hooks.

styles.name: Sierreño
styles.description: Guitar-and-tuba Sinaloan/Sierra style; Los Dareyes de la Sierra, Ariel Camacho (later)

styles.name: Folk Punk
styles.description: US DIY acoustic punk around Plan-It-X (Bloomington, IN); Against Me!, AJJ, Defiance Ohio; later YouTube wave (Days N' Daze)

styles.name: Nerdcore
styles.description: The reference as a voice, dense rhyming about games, code and fandom.

styles.name: Hauntology
styles.description: UK; Ghost Box label (Belbury Poly, The Focus Group), The Caretaker, Burial; term from Fisher/Reynolds

styles.name: Retro Soul
styles.description: Recorded as if it were 1966, analog tape, live horns and a band playing together in one room.

styles.name: Vocaloid / Miku Pop
styles.description: Japan; Hatsune Miku + Niconico producer scene (supercell, livetune, wowaka); US via Miku Expo tours, Coachella 2024

styles.name: Easycore
styles.description: The chorus landing in the breakdown, pop punk hooks spliced into hardcore heaviness.

styles.name: Future Garage
styles.description: UK; named by Whistla 2009; Burial-style 2-step swing with ambient haze; Hyperdub

styles.name: Electro Swing
styles.description: European sampled-swing dance music; Parov Stelar, Caravan Palace; 'We No Speak Americano' hit the US Hot 100 (2010)

styles.name: Afro House
styles.description: South Africa (Black Coffee, Culoe De Song, Black Motion); Beatport category 2017; US via Keinemusik, 'Jerusalema', MSG 2023

styles.name: Tribal Guarachero
styles.description: Mexico City pre-Hispanic-sample club music that broke out of Monterrey; 3Ball MTY 'Inténtalo', pointy-boot dance craze in Texas/Mexico

styles.name: Dungeon Synth
styles.description: Lo-fi medieval-fantasy keyboard music from black metal (Mortiis, Burzum); named 2011 on The Dungeon Synth Blog; Bandcamp boom: Old Tower, Erang, Fief

styles.name: Gqom
styles.description: Durban; DJ Lag, Rudeboyz, Distruction Boyz; Gqom Oh! label; DJ Lag on Beyoncé's 'My Power' (2019)

styles.name: Chicago Bop
styles.description: Bright synth loops, springy fast drums and exuberant Auto-Tuned voices leave room for elbows, knees and whole-body turns. Short hooks behave like dance instructions.

styles.name: Future House
styles.description: Term coined by Tchami (2013); Oliver Heldens 'Gecko', Don Diablo; Spinnin'/Hexagon; US radio via Martin Solveig

styles.name: Grungegaze
styles.description: Weight turned into atmosphere, grunge's heaviness played through shoegaze's wash.

styles.name: Dissonant Death Metal
styles.description: Atonal, atmospheric death metal after Gorguts' Obscura/Coloured Sands: Ulcerate (NZ), Portal, Deathspell Omega-influenced; 'dissodeath'

styles.name: Deconstructed Club
styles.description: NYC GHE20G0TH1K parties, Fade to Mind (LA), NAAFI, PAN; Arca, Total Freedom, Elysia Crampton

styles.name: Bass House / G-House
styles.description: US/UK; Jauz, AC Slater's Night Bass (LA), Joyryde, Habstrakt; dubstep-weight basslines on house

styles.name: Riddim (dubstep)
styles.description: Croydon roots (Jakes, Subfiltronik); US bass-scene adoption c.2015, Lost Lands; Virtual Riot, Svdden Death

styles.name: Melodic Techno
styles.description: Berlin/Milan; Tale of Us' Afterlife (2016), Stephan Bodzin, ARTBAT; US arena scale via Anyma Sphere residency

styles.name: Guaracha / Aleteo
styles.description: Medellín; Víctor Cárdenas, DJ Pereira; cumbia brass over tech-house kicks; Latino club staple in US

styles.name: Alté
styles.description: Lagos; DRB LasGidi coined term; Cruel Santino, Odunsi (The Engine), Lady Donli; feeder for Tems, Amaarae

styles.name: Trap Metal
styles.description: Screamed vocals and distorted 808s over trap beats: Scarlxrd, Ghostemane, City Morgue/ZillaKami; also 'ragecore', 'death rap'

styles.name: Neoperreo
styles.description: DIY voices bend reggaeton’s dembow through distorted bass, eerie synths and playful digital textures. Intimate, confrontational hooks turn a familiar dance rhythm into personal territory.

styles.name: Egg Punk
styles.description: The wrong shape made to fit, cheap synths and tinny recording behind deliberately awkward punk songs.

styles.name: UK Jazz (South London Scene)
styles.description: Tomorrow's Warriors alumni, Steam Down (Deptford), We Out Here comp; Shabaka Hutchings/Sons of Kemet, Nubya Garcia, Ezra Collective

styles.name: Slap House
styles.description: Brazilian bass (Alok) pared down by Imanbek (Kazakhstan); 'Roses' remix US #4; Dynoro, VIZE, Tiësto 'The Business'

styles.name: Milwaukee Lowend
styles.description: Fast claps, heavy bass and tiny loops make a restless dance floor. Deadpan rap and tender singing pull against the frantic pulse.

styles.name: Sigilkore
styles.description: Occult-themed SoundCloud/TikTok mixing style coined by Luci4 and the Jewelxxet collective; Odetari, 9lives, Lumi Athena

styles.name: Dariacore / Hyperflip
styles.description: Familiar pop fragments collide with rushing synth drops, chopped breaks and lurching club kicks. Abrupt cuts turn recognition into a new dance structure.

styles.name: 3-Step
styles.description: Johannesburg; three kicks per bar; Thakzin 'The Magnificent Dance', Dlala Thukzin 'iPlan', Mörda & Oscar Mbo 'Yes God'

crossStylePlaylists.title: Halloween for the Weirdos
crossStylePlaylists.about: Ninety years of monster records, from séance swing to the Cramps

crossStylePlaylists.title: Someone Else’s Story
crossStylePlaylists.about: Andy Shauf writes in other people’s voices, and the songwriters who taught him how
